source_text: Diximus paulo ante in principio regni sancti fore ut a deo princeps daemonum uinciatur. sed idem, cum mille anni regni hoc est septem milia coeperint terminari, soluetur denuo et custodia emissus exibit atque omnes gentes quae tunc erunt sub dicione iustorum concitabit, ut inferant bellum sanctae ciuitati. et colligetur ex omni orbe terrae innumerabilis populus nationum et obsidebit et circumdabit ciuitatem. tum ueniet nouissima ira dei super gentes, et debellabit eas usque ad unum. ac primum concutiet terram quam ualidissime et a motu eius scindentur montes Syriae et subsident ualles in abruptum et muri omnium ciuitatum concident. et statuet deus solem triduo ne occidat et inflammabit eum, et descendet aestus nimius et adustio magna super perduelles et impios populos et imbres sulphuris et grandines lapidum et guttae ignis, et liquescent spiritus eorum in calore et corpora conterentur in grandine et ipsi se inuicem gladio ferient: et replebuntur montes cadaueribus et campi operientur ossibus. populus autem dei tribus illis diebus sub concauis terrae occultabitur, donec ira dei aduersus gentes et extremum indicium terminetur. tunc exibunt iusti de latebus suis et inuenient omnia cadaueribus atque ossibus tecta. sed et genus omne impiorum radicitus interibit nec erit in hoc mundo ulla iam natio amplius praeter solam gentem dei. tum per annos septem perpetes intactae erunt siluae nec excidetur de montibus lignum, sed arma gentium comburentur, et iam non erit bellum, sed pax ac requies sempiterna. cum uero conpleti fuerint mille anni, renouabitur mundus a deo et caelum conplicabitur et terra mutabitur. et transformabit deus homines in similitudinem angelorum et erunt candidi sicut nix et uersabuntur semper in conspectu omnipotentis et domino suo sacrificabunt et seruient in aeternum. eodem tempore fiet secunda illa et publica omnium resurrectio, in qua excitabuntur iniusti ad cruciatus sempiternos. hi sunt qui manu facta coluerunt, qui dominum mundi ac parentem uel nescierunt uel abnegauerunt. sed et dominus illorum cum ministris suis conprehendetur ad poenamque damnabitur, cum quo pariter omnis turba impiorum pro suis facinoribus in conspectu angelorum atque iustorum perpetuo igni cremabitur in aeternum. haec est doctrina sanctorum prophetarum, quam Christiani sequimur, haec nostra sapientia, quam isti qui uel fragilia colunt uel inanem philosophiam tuentur, tamquam stultitiam uanitatemque derident, quia nos defendere hanc publice atque adserere non solemus, deo iubente ut quieti ac silentes arcanum eius in abdito atque intra nostram conscientiam teneamus nec aduersus istos ueri profanos, qui non discendi, sed arguendi atque inludendi gratia inclementer deum ac religionem eius inpugnant, pertinaci contentione certemus. abscondi enim tegique mysterium quam fidelissime oportet, maxime a nobis, qui nomen fidei gerimus. uerum illi hanc taciturnitatem nostram ueluti malam conscientiam criminantur: unde etiam quasdam exsecrabiles opiniones de pudicis et innocentibus fingunt et libenter iis quae finxerint credunt.
pass_a_gloss: We said a little while ago at the beginning of the holy kingdom that the prince of demons will be conquered by God. But the same one, when the thousand years of this kingdom, that is seven thousand, have begun to come to an end, will be loosed again and, having been released from custody, will go out and will stir up all the nations which will then be under the rule of the just, so that they may bring war against the holy city. And an innumerable people of nations will be gathered from the whole earth and will besiege and surround the city. Then the final wrath of God will come upon the nations, and He will war against them until not one is left. And first He will shake the earth most violently and from its motion the mountains of Syria will be torn apart and the valleys will sink down abruptly and the walls of all the cities will fall. And God will station the sun for three days so that it does not set and will set it on fire, and an immense heat and great burning will come down upon the perverted and impious peoples and there will be showers of sulphur and hail of stones and drops of fire, and their spirits will melt away in the heat and their bodies will be crushed in the hail and they will strike one another with the sword. And the mountains will be filled with corpses and the fields will be covered with bones. But the people of God will be hidden under the hollows of the earth for those three days, until the wrath of God against the nations and the final judgment come to an end. Then the just will come out from their hiding places and will find all things covered with corpses and bones. But also the whole race of the impious will perish root and branch and there will not be any nation left in this world except the nation of God alone. Then for seven years the forests will remain uncut and no tree will be cut down from the mountains, but the arms of the nations will be burned, and there will no longer be war, but eternal peace and rest. When the thousand years have been completed, the world will be renewed by God and the heaven will be folded up and the earth will be changed. And God will transform humans into the likeness of angels and they will be white as snow and will always be turned towards the face of the Omnipotent and will sacrifice to and serve their Lord forever. At the same time, that second and public resurrection of all will take place, in which the unjust will be raised up for eternal torments. These are the ones who worshipped things made by hand, who either did not know or denied the Lord of the world and their parent. But also their lord with his servants will be seized for punishment and will be condemned, and with him all the crowd of the impious will be burned in eternal fire in the presence of the angels and the just for their own deeds. This is the doctrine of the holy prophets, which Christians follow, this is our wisdom, which those who worship fragile things or defend empty philosophy deride as foolishness and vanity, because we are not accustomed to defend this publicly and to assert it, God commanding that we keep His secret in silence and in our own conscience and not contend with those profane people who do not learn but argue and mock God and His religion inclemently. For the mystery ought to be hidden and concealed most faithfully, especially by us who bear the name of faith. But those people accuse our silence as if it were a bad conscience: whence they also invent some execrable opinions about chaste and innocent people and gladly believe the things they have invented.

pass_b_english: We noted a little earlier that when the holy kingdom begins, God will conquer the prince of demons. But once the thousand years of that kingdom — seven thousand in total — begin to draw to a close, he will be loosed once more. Released from custody, he will go out and incite every nation then under the rule of the just, so that they wage war against the holy city. An innumerable host of nations will be gathered from the whole earth and will besiege and surround the city. Then the final wrath of God will fall upon the nations, and He will war against them until not one remains. First He will shake the earth with terrible force; from that convulsion the mountains of Syria will be torn apart, valleys will plunge downward abruptly, and the walls of every city will collapse. God will station the sun for three days so that it does not set, and He will set it ablaze. An immense heat and a great burning will descend upon the perverse and impious peoples. Showers of sulphur, hailstones, and drops of fire will fall. Their spirits will melt away in the heat, their bodies will be crushed by the hail, and they will turn their swords against one another. Mountains will be filled with corpses, fields covered with bones. But for those three days the people of God will be hidden in the hollows of the earth, until God's wrath against the nations and the final judgment have run their course. Then the just will emerge from their hiding places and find everything blanketed with corpses and bones. The entire race of the impious will perish root and branch, and no nation will remain in this world except the nation of God alone. For seven years the forests will stand uncut, no tree felled from the mountains; the weapons of the nations will be burned, and war will be no more, but eternal peace and rest. When the thousand years are completed, God will renew the world: the heavens will be rolled up and the earth transformed. God will transform human beings into the likeness of angels; they will be white as snow and will live ever in the presence of the Omnipotent, sacrificing to and serving their Lord forever. At that same time the second, public resurrection of all will take place, and the unjust will be raised for eternal torments. These are the ones who worshipped things made by hand, who either did not know or denied the Lord of the world and their Father. Their lord, together with his servants, will be seized for punishment and condemned, and with him the whole throng of the impious will be burned in eternal fire before the angels and the just for their own deeds. This is the doctrine of the holy prophets, which Christians follow; this is our wisdom. Those who worship fragile things or defend empty philosophy deride it as foolishness and vanity, because we are not accustomed to defend or assert it publicly. God commands that we keep His secret in silence and within our own conscience, and not contend with those profane people who attack God and His religion inclemently, not to learn but to argue and mock. The mystery must be hidden and concealed most faithfully, especially by us who bear the name of faith. Yet they accuse our silence as if it were a guilty conscience; from that they invent execrable opinions about chaste and innocent people and gladly believe their own inventions.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the eschatological sequence and the theological nuances of the Latin text. Pass A preserves the clause structure and nuances (e.g., 'in the face of the Omnipotent' for 'in conspectu omnipotentis'), while Pass B provides a fluent rendering that does not contradict the source. All theological distinctions regarding the thousand years, the nature of the resurrection, and the Christian stance on silence are maintained.

The translation accurately reflects the Latin text, preserving the meaning, structure, and key theological concepts. The inline citations are correctly matched to the content, and the translation adheres to the source text without adding or omitting significant content. The title 'Destruction and Renewal' appropriately captures the central theme of the passage.
